name: 12-3-30 incline walking
lead: The 12-3-30 workout is a treadmill routine named for its settings: a 12 percent incline, a speed of 3 miles per hour and 30 minutes of walking. It spread through social media and is discussed in looksmaxxing and fitness circles as a low-impact fat-loss routine.

Published research is very limited: a 2025 exploratory study in the International Journal of Exercise Science compared the metabolic responses of the 12-3-30 workout with self-paced treadmill running.[1]

paras: An exploratory study published in 2025 compared the metabolic responses between the 12-3-30 treadmill workout and self-paced treadmill running.[1] The sources reviewed did not allow the study's detailed findings to be summarised here. No trials have been identified that test 12-3-30 for fat loss or appearance outcomes.

lore.intro: The routine is circulated as a viral, low-impact alternative to running; claims below reflect that general framing, not specific threads.

claims.believers: Proponents say it is accessible and joint-friendly.
claims.experts: No published trial has tested it for fat loss; the only study found compared metabolic responses with running.[1]

refs.title: An Exploratory Study Comparing the Metabolic Responses between the 12-3-30 Treadmill Workout and Self-Paced Treadmill Running

card.summary: Viral 12% incline, 3 mph, 30 minute treadmill walk; only one small exploratory study exists.
card.note: Little published research on fat-loss outcomes.

quick.overview:
A treadmill routine: 12 percent incline, 3 mph, 30 minutes.

It went viral on social media; one exploratory 2025 study has examined its metabolic responses.
quick.mechanism: Walking on a steep incline raises the effort of walking without the impact of running.
quick.risks: Generally considered low-risk; steep inclines can strain calves or ankles for some people.
